answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it may vote or claim rewards, then slash that stake when a challenge proves coordinated duplicate control. This does not make identities impossible to fake; it makes influence costly: an attacker must acquire and risk capital for every Sybil, while honest agents can pool evidence to trigger review. Like a tide crossing tundra and karst, the attack may spread, but each foothold has a price.
